expectations.text: GOVERN function added (elevating governance/supply-chain risk strategy), reorganizing former ID categories
expectations.evidence: CSF 2.0 adds Govern as a sixth... Much of Govern's content existed in 1.1 but was scattered - parts lived under Identify (ID.GV, ID.RM, ID.SC in 1.1)

expectations.text: Scope broadened: from critical infrastructure to all organizations
expectations.evidence: CSF 1.1 was explicitly framed around critical infrastructure. CSF 2.0 drops that framing and positions itself as applicable to any organization, regardless of sector or size

expectations.text: Structural changes: categories/subcategories reorganized and renumbered — requires subcategory-level remapping, not a rename
expectations.evidence: Subcategory reorganization and renumbering... You cannot assume a simple ID-to-ID renumbering; you need to actually re-read the new subcategory language

expectations.text: Mentions new support resources: implementation examples, quick-start guides, reference tool, community profiles
expectations.evidence: Introduces 'Community Profiles', 'Implementation Examples', and the 'online Cybersecurity and Privacy Reference Tool (CPRT)'

expectations.text: Gives a sane migration path: map existing 1.1 profile to 2.0 subcategories, stand up GOVERN outcomes, refresh target profile and roadmap
expectations.evidence: Step 1 - Map your existing 1.1 profile... using NIST's published 1.1-to-2.0 crosswalk. Step 2 - Stand up Govern... Step 4 - Rebuild your Current Profile... Step 5 - Reset your Target Profile
